questions.question: Prove by contradiction that √2 is irrational.
questions.questionText: Prove by contradiction that √2 is irrational.
steps: 1. Assume √2 = a/b in lowest terms with integers a, b and b ≠ 0. Then a² = 2b².
2. Thus a is even; write a = 2k. Substitution gives b² = 2k², so b is even.
3. Both a and b are even, contradicting that the fraction was in lowest terms.

questions.question: Prove by contradiction that there are infinitely many primes.

2. The integer N = p₁p₂…pₙ + 1 exceeds 1 and is not divisible by any listed prime.
3. N has a prime divisor outside the list, contradicting completeness.

questions.question: Prove by contradiction that √3 is irrational.
questions.questionText: Prove by contradiction that √3 is irrational.
steps: 1. Assume √3 = a/b in lowest terms, so a² = 3b².
2. An integer square divisible by 3 has its base divisible by 3. Write a = 3k; then b² = 3k², so 3 also divides b.
